questiontext.text: What is the defining capability of a leftist heap?

answer.text: Efficiently merging (melding) two heaps in O(log n)

feedback.text: Correct — leftist heaps are mergeable heaps built around a fast meld.

answer.text: O(1) worst-case extract-min

feedback.text: No — extract-min is O(log n), built on top of merge.

answer.text: Storing keys in a flat array without pointers

feedback.text: No — leftist heaps are pointer-based binary trees.

answer.text: Keeping elements in fully sorted order

feedback.text: No — it only maintains the heap-order property.

generalfeedback.text: A leftist heap is a mergeable (meldable) heap whose signature operation is O(log n) merge; insert and extract-min are expressed via merge.

questiontext.text: The leftist property is stated in terms of which per-node quantity?

answer.text: The null-path length (s-value): distance to the nearest null descendant

feedback.text: Correct — the s-value drives the leftist invariant.

answer.text: The subtree size (number of nodes)

feedback.text: No — leftist heaps balance on path length, not size.

answer.text: The node's key value

feedback.text: No — that governs heap order, not the leftist shape.

answer.text: The node's color (red or black)

feedback.text: No — that belongs to red-black trees.

generalfeedback.text: Each node stores its null-path length (s-value), the distance to the closest missing child; the leftist property compares s-values of the two children.

questiontext.text: The leftist property requires that, for every node:

answer.text: The left child's s-value is ≥ the right child's s-value

feedback.text: Correct — this keeps the short spine on the right.

answer.text: The left child's key is ≤ the right child's key

feedback.text: No — that is not the leftist property; siblings are unordered.

answer.text: Both subtrees have equal height

feedback.text: No — leftist heaps are deliberately unbalanced.

answer.text: The right child must be null

feedback.text: No — the right spine is short but not necessarily empty.

generalfeedback.text: For every node, s(left) ≥ s(right); this pushes the shortest path to the right, keeping the right spine O(log n).

questiontext.text: Why can leftist-heap merge run in O(log n)?

answer.text: Merging only walks the two right spines, and each right spine has length O(log n)

feedback.text: Correct — the leftist property bounds the right spine, so merge is logarithmic.

answer.text: Because it copies both heaps into a sorted array first

feedback.text: No — merge is done in place along the right paths, no array copy.

answer.text: Because the tree is perfectly balanced

feedback.text: No — leftist heaps are not height-balanced.

answer.text: Because every node has O(1) children to visit

feedback.text: Bounded children alone would not bound total work; the short right spine does.

generalfeedback.text: Merge recurses down the two right spines; the leftist invariant guarantees each right spine is O(log n), so merge is O(log n).

questiontext.text: In a leftist heap, both insert and extract-min are implemented as special cases of merge.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — insert merges a one-node heap; extract-min merges the root's two children.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Both are expressed via merge: insert melds a singleton, extract-min melds the two subtrees.

questiontext.text: A leftist heap is a height-balanced tree in which the left and right subtrees have nearly equal height.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — it is intentionally unbalanced, biased so the right spine stays short.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — leftist heaps are deliberately lopsided, not height-balanced.

questiontext.text: The single core operation on which a leftist heap's insert and delete-min are built is called ______ (also known as meld).

answer.text: merge

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: merge*

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: meld

feedback.text: Correct — meld is a synonym.

answer.text: meld*

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about a leftist heap are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: It is a mergeable (meldable) heap supporting O(log n) merge

feedback.text: Yes — that is its defining feature.

answer.text: Each node stores a null-path-length (s-value) used to maintain the invariant

feedback.text: Yes — the s-value is the bookkeeping it maintains.

answer.text: It is stored in an implicit array like a binary heap

feedback.text: No — it is a pointer-linked binary tree, not an implicit array.

answer.text: Its two subtrees are kept balanced in height

feedback.text: No — it is biased so the right spine stays short, not balanced.

generalfeedback.text: A leftist heap is a pointer-based mergeable heap: O(log n) merge, per-node s-values, and an intentionally lopsided (short right spine) shape rather than height balance.
